description: Mitigations for fall from height. Ordered by hierarchy: design → engineered → managed. Pre-impact and post-impact separated.

mitigations.name: elimination_of_height
mitigations.description: Design out the need to work at height. Prefabrication at ground level, remote inspection (drones), permanent access platforms.
mitigations.pfd_source: Inherent safety — if work at height is eliminated, the hazard doesn't exist. PFD reflects rare cases where elimination isn't complete.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: By definition, eliminating the fall hazard removes the energy source.

mitigations.name: guardrail
mitigations.description: Fixed edge protection preventing access to fall zone. EN 13374 temporary edge protection, permanent guardrails. Passive — no human action required.
mitigations.pfd_source: LOPA: PFD 0.01-0.02 for passive engineered barriers. Failure modes: incomplete installation, gap in coverage, structural failure under load.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: When present and intact, guardrails prevent >95% of falls over the edge. P10 reflects cases where worker climbs over or guardrail doesn't cover all edges.

mitigations.name: safety_net
mitigations.description: Collective fall arrest net below the working level. EN 1263 safety nets. Catches the person during the fall — reduces impact energy.
mitigations.pfd_source: LOPA: PFD 0.02-0.03. Failure modes: incorrect mesh size, deterioration, gap at edges, excessive fall distance into net.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: ANSI Z359.2 test data. Safety nets limit fall distance and decelerate the body. Residual injury from net impact is typically P(death) < 0.005. P10 reflects cases near net edge or excessive fall height before net engagement.

mitigations.name: harness_lanyard
mitigations.description: Personal fall arrest system: full body harness + energy-absorbing lanyard + anchor point. EN 361/EN 355. Requires the worker to clip on — human-dependent.
mitigations.pfd_source: LOPA: PFD 0.05 for PPE requiring human action. Failure modes: not clipped on (most common — worker forgets or finds it inconvenient), incorrect anchor point, damaged lanyard, insufficient free-fall clearance. HSE data: ~5% non-compliance rate even on monitored sites.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: When properly worn and anchored, arrests the fall. Residual injury from suspension trauma, harness impact forces (EN 355 limits to 6kN). P(death) < 0.01 when system works correctly.

mitigations.name: work_restraint
mitigations.description: Short lanyard or retractable preventing the worker from reaching the fall edge. Better than fall arrest because the fall never starts. Requires correct anchor and lanyard length.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.07 — same human-dependent failure as harness, plus incorrect lanyard length allowing edge access. Slightly less reliable than fall arrest because length calculation must be correct.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: When correctly configured, prevents reaching the edge. Near-complete elimination of fall risk. Higher effectiveness than fall arrest because no fall occurs.

mitigations.name: permit_to_work
mitigations.description: Administrative control requiring formal authorisation before work at height. Ensures risk assessment, equipment check, and competent person review. Does not physically prevent the fall.
mitigations.pfd_source: LOPA: PFD 0.10 for administrative controls. Failure modes: permit not obtained (work done informally), risk assessment inadequate, permit conditions not followed on site.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: A permit doesn't stop a fall — it ensures other controls are in place. Effectiveness is indirect: the probability that the permit process results in adequate physical controls being implemented.

mitigations.name: rescue_plan
mitigations.description: Post-fall rescue plan with trained team, equipment, and rehearsal. Critical for suspended worker after fall arrest (suspension trauma kills within 30 min). Also covers rescue from height for injured worker.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.15 — human-dependent, requires team availability, equipment readiness, and rehearsal. Failure: no rescue plan, team not on site, equipment not maintained.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Prompt rescue (within 15 min) of a suspended worker prevents suspension trauma death. Effectiveness is time-dependent — 90% survival if rescued in <10 min, dropping rapidly after 20 min.
